verdicts.title: About page's GitHub and Documentation links are placeholders that 404 / do not resolve
verdicts.reasoning: Verified independently at the source and over the network. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/about_settings.dart hard-codes the three URLs twice (mobile Wrap at :102/:109/:116, desktop Row at :128/:135/:142) exactly as the finding states -- the cited line numbers are correct for the mobile branch and the finding correctly names the desktop duplicates too. Network checks I ran myself: curl https://github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404; curl https://github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq -> 200; getent hosts skotiq.astro -> no answer (.astro is not a delegated TLD, so the Documentation button can never resolve). The Discord claim is also true but for a different reason than 'not an invite': https://discord.gg/skotiq 301s to discord.com/invite/skotiq and the Discord API returns a VALID invite -- to guild 1370106030754631690, 'Skotiq Gaming Community', an unrelated gaming server. So the button works and lands the user in a stranger's gaming Discord, which is worse than a dead link, not better. Note the app's _launchUrl only reports failure when canLaunchUrl/launchUrl returns false, which a 404 page does not, so the finding's 'no error banner' observation is correct by construction.

verdicts.title: Paired devices live in ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db -- outside the app database, outside the configured data dir, and split across two stores
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from scratch on my own display. I started --fresh with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/v-settings-system/data, skipped onboarding, and opened Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing: the dialog immediately listed 13 devices with paired dates 6/15/2026, 7/20/2026 x3, 7/22, 7/25 x3, 7/26 -- pairings months older than this profile. sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/v-settings-system/data/skotiq.db '.tables' has NO pairing table at all; sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) from paired_devices where is_active=1' returns 13, matching the UI count exactly and the names row-for-row (Dashboard, Android companion x4, Browser, ui-audit-avd, LAN device, Lead Harness, audit-probe). (The finding said 12; it is 13 now because other audit agents paired since -- the count tracks the shared store, which is itself the point.) The cited location is exactly right: pairing_database.dart:401-410 is LazyDatabase _openConnection() { final dbFolder = await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory(); final file = File(p.join(dbFolder.path, 'Skotiq', 'pairing.db')); ... } -- no data-dir override is consulted anywhere. The two-store claim also holds: ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db (40KB, mtime Aug 1, 13 active rows) and ~/Skotiq/pairing.db (40KB, mtime Jul 29, 0 rows) both exist on this machine from the same install.

verdicts.title: Backups are written to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups regardless of the configured data directory, so bundles from different databases pile into one undifferentiated 'Recent Backups' list
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on a first-ever launch of profile v-settings-system (--fresh, SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/v-settings-system/data, equipment_profiles empty). Settings > Backup & Restore came up with a NON-EMPTY 'Recent Backups' list -- 9 bundles dated Aug 1 and Aug 2 that this profile never created -- and 'Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 12:03'. Merely opening the screen also WROTE into the shared directory: ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups gained skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T12-03-46/47/48, and their metadata is my throwaway database (settingsCount 121, profilesCount 0), sitting in the same list as the developer's real 7.0 KB bundles. A fourth file appeared at 12-03-53 with profilesCount 1 while my DB still had zero profiles -- i.e. a CONCURRENT audit instance on another display wrote into the same list at the same time, which is the finding's 'two installs' scenario happening live. `find /tmp/ns-audit/v-settings-system -iname '*backup*'` returns nothing, so nothing was written under the configured data dir. Root cause located precisely: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/backup_service.dart:1025-1030, _getBackupDirectory() -> getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups; the _backupDirectoryProvider override on line 121/149 is referenced from exactly one place in the repo, test/services/backup_service_listing_test.dart:34, so production has no data-dir-aware path at all. The two-directory claim holds too (~/Documents/Skotiq/backups: 9 bundles, ~/Skotiq/backups: 4). The 'nothing in the row says which database it came from' claim is accurate -- rows render name + size + date only.

verdicts.title: A profile saved without optics can never be edited again: Save is rejected because of the 0 the app itself stored, and the rejection is invisible on screen
verdicts.reasoning: SYMPTOM CONFIRMED, STATED CAUSE HALF WRONG -- the 'invisible' half is false and it is what inflated this to P1. What I reproduced exactly: Settings > Equipment Profiles > New Profile 'VSS Rig A' > Create wrote id=1, focal_length=0.0, aperture=0.0. Re-opening it, the Edit form pre-fills the two optics fields with a literal '0'. Changing only the name to 'VSS Renamed B' and pressing Save leaves the DB untouched (sqlite3 still returned 1|VSS Rig A|0.0|0.0 after repeated attempts). Clearing BOTH optics fields let the same save through -- and stored 0.0/0.0 again (1|VSS Renamed B|0.0|0.0), so the profile is immediately back in the rejecting state. The loop is exact in code: equipment_profile_validation.dart:_parseOptic returns ok(0.0) for blank but fail('<label> must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)') for any parsed value <= 0, while the model stores blank as the 0 sentinel and the editor renders that sentinel as '0'. WHAT IS REFUTED: 'nothing happens... no banner... the button appears dead... a full-window screenshot shows no such text anywhere on screen'. It does show. I burst-captured the root window every 250 ms across the Save click and diffed against a baseline: frames 1-2 show only the status-bar clock changing, and from frame 3 (~0.5 s after the click) a full-width red SnackBar occupies y=970..1039 carrying both messages, fully legible, and stays for the 4 s duration (crop: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vss-snackregion.png). The earlier agent's screenshot was taken inside the snackbar's ~0.5 s entrance latency -- I made the identical mistake once with drive_linux.py shot before switching to burst capture. The finding's secondary claim IS right: there is no field-level error and no colour change on the offending fields (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vss-opticsrow.png -- both boxes render plain '0' with normal borders during the rejection). Location: the cited profile_details.dart:175-200 is slightly off; the optics parse is at :170 and :172 and the error surface is context.showErrorSnackBar(errors.join('\n')) at :219, inside _validateAndBuild (:167-248). Downgraded to P2: the user is told exactly what to do ('leave blank if unknown') in a visible banner, so this is a self-inflicted round-trip trap, not silent data loss.
verdicts.location_wrong: profile_details.dart:175-200 -- the optics validators are at :170/:172, the error is raised at :219; the whole function is :167-248

verdicts.title: Restore silently drops a backed-up equipment profile when its row id is already taken, and still reports 'Restored 123 items'
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with my own bundle, plus the control case, plus the exact code path. Setup: profile id=1 'VSS Renamed B' -> Create Backup produced skotiq_backup_2026-08-02T12-13-00.755211.nsbackup, whose equipmentProfiles[0] is {id:1, name:'VSS Renamed B'} and whose metadata is settingsCount 122 / profilesCount 1 = 123. I then renamed row id 1 locally to 'VSS Local Keep' and restored that bundle from Recent Backups. Burst capture of the toast reads verbatim 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vss-restoretoast.png), and sqlite3 afterwards returns 1|VSS Local Keep|0.0|0.0 -- 'VSS Renamed B' was neither inserted nor applied over row 1. CONTROL CASE: I deleted the profile (equipment_profiles empty) and restored the SAME bundle; it came back as 1|VSS Renamed B. So the discriminator is the id collision, exactly as claimed. Code confirms the mechanism and sharpens the 'where': the real location is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/backup_service/sequence_codec.dart:_importProfiles -- it inserts with the BACKUP's row id (id: Value(_intOrDefault(profile['id'], 0)) at :50-52) using mode: replace ? InsertMode.replace : InsertMode.insertOrIgnore at :114, and then does count++ at :116 UNCONDITIONALLY, so the returned count is 'rows attempted', not 'rows written'. backup_screen.dart:265-267 always calls restoreBackup(replaceExisting: false), so the UI can only ever take the insertOrIgnore branch. restoreBackup then sums those attempted-counts into itemsRestored (backup_service.dart:437-453) and the screen prints it at :275. One nuance the finding does not mention, in the app's favour: the confirm dialog hedges with 'library items from the backup MAY be added' -- but the toast afterwards states a definite count that it never checked, so the claim is still false. Keeping P1: a restore feature that reports success for data it silently dropped is exactly the class of untrue-statement defect this project treats as ship-blocking.
verdicts.location_wrong: cited only as 'the restore path in the backup service ... called from backup_screen.dart'; the actual defect lines are sequence_codec.dart:50-52, :114 and :116 (id-keyed insertOrIgnore + unconditional count++), with backup_screen.dart:267 forcing replaceExisting:false and :275 printing the count

verdicts.title: Every Settings snackbar renders underneath the persistent bottom status bar, so all success and failure feedback in Settings is invisible
verdicts.reasoning: The snackbars are visible. I measured it rather than eyeballing it: xdotool click on the control, then `import -window root` every 250-300 ms, then a numpy pixel diff of each frame against a pre-click baseline. Case 1, the rejected profile Save (finding 3's case): frames 1-2 show ONLY the status-bar clock digits changing (bbox y1027-1036, x1671-1677); from frame 3 onward a full-width bar occupies y=970..1039, x=175..1744 -- 109,872 changed pixels. Cropping it (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vss-snackregion.png) gives a red SnackBar reading 'Focal length must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown) / Aperture must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)', fully legible, persisting across all remaining frames of its 4 s duration. Case 2, the restore toast (finding 5's case): same method, same geometry, a green bar reading 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vss-restoretoast.png). The stated cause is backwards: the app window is 160,150..1760,1050 and the status bar occupies roughly y1019..1050, so the snackbar OVERLAPS it -- and it is painted ON TOP, covering the status bar, not under it. Structurally that is what Flutter does here: app_shell.dart:633-816 puts StatusBar(compact:false) as the last child of the shell Scaffold's body Column with no bottomNavigationBar, and Scaffold paints the _ScaffoldSlot.snackBar after the body. What actually produced the original observation is a ~0.5 s gap between the click and the snackbar's first painted frame (entrance animation on a softpipe renderer): every capture taken inside that window shows nothing while a `tree` read a second later still finds the message. I reproduced that false negative myself with drive_linux.py shot before switching to burst capture, so this is a harness artefact, not a defect. Residual real issue, worth P3 at most: while shown, the snackbar hides the status bar (Idle/profile/device pills/LST), and TransientBottomInset -- the mechanism built exactly to prevent that (utils/snackbar_helper.dart:20-27) -- is published by only one screen in the whole app, imaging_screen.dart:153. Also note this finding duplicates the 'invisible rejection' half of finding 3; both rest on the same mis-timed screenshot.
